clue.text: Fish got left in the straw

indicators.note: the word left is set inside the hat named by the straw

parts.note: a boater is a stiff straw hat

explanation.surface: Someone's catch was left lying in the straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got ... in' puts L inside BOATER, a flat-topped straw hat once worn for boating.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring that has been salted and smoked whole.

clue.text: Extravagant King of Naples gets son endless credit

parts.note: King Bomba was the nickname of Ferdinand II of the Two Sicilies, ruler of Naples

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for credit is cut

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, buying on tick

explanation.surface: A lavish monarch of Naples gives his son unlimited credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts TICK to TIC; 'on tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic means high-flown and inflated in speech, extravagant in style.

clue.text: After work return it to mother — that's best

indicators.note: after says the reversed word follows the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: return means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
mum is mother

explanation.surface: Once the job is done, give it back to Mum: that is ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable, ideal condition.

clue.text: Where martyrs were led up and told to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to re-form, so the letters are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: Protesters were marched off and ordered to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tolpuddle Martyrs were Dorset farm labourers transported in 1834 for forming a union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset village gave its name to labourers punished for organising a trade union.

clue.text: Care, perhaps, for a bit of ginger?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the given word is one rearrangement among others

explanation.surface: Is caution needed with a little spice?
explanation.definitionFit: A race of ginger is a root or piece of the spice rhizome.

clue.text: She's written article about sex-appeal

parts.note: the definite article is the word the
re is Latin-derived for concerning, about
SA is an old abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A woman has penned a piece on sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: a woman's name, with ''s written' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Go. rap hatch. disturbing the spy in the cab

indicators.note: disturbing tells us to throw these letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone told to go and knock at a hatch, upsetting a spy in a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: A spy in the cab is the nickname for a device in a lorry cab recording speed and hours.
explanation.definitionFit: This recorder logs a driver's speed and rest periods, so drivers call it a spy.

clue.text: To some a weird sound from this nest?

indicators.note: to some people the word is pronounced alike, a hint about speech
sound tells us the word for weird is matched by ear

parts.note: eerie means weird, strange

explanation.surface: A strange noise coming from a nest strikes some as uncanny.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the lofty nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: As an excuse raised a rumpus about state shortage?

indicators.note: about places the reversed word round the short state name
raised in a down clue means the word for rumpus is read upwards

parts.note: a rumpus is a din, a noise
a state shortage is a state's abbreviation: VA for Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss over a national shortfall, by way of excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NOISE into ESION; 'about' puts it round VA, 'state shortage' meaning an abbreviated US state.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasion is a dodge or pretext used to avoid something.

clue.text: Woody is looking pale

definitions.meaning: made of the wood of a common tree

explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a timber tree, so ash-en means made of it; a wan face is grey as cinders.

clue.text: Roadhouse where carousers dropping round spend the night

definitions.text: Roadhouse where carousers dropping round spend the night

parts.words: Roadhouse where carousers dropping round spend the night
parts.note: split carousers as car-ousers, car users: motorists who drop in at a roadside inn to sleep

explanation.surface: Revellers stagger round to a roadside inn and stay the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carousers' suggests drinkers, but read it as 'car users', drivers calling in for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel built for travelling drivers, who park beside their rooms overnight.

clue.text: Vermin found in bird and fish

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
the roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Pests discovered inside a bird and a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is a common household pest, counted among vermin.

clue.text: Protective clothing for night-fighter, say

parts.note: night-fighter sounds like knight-fighter, a mounted warrior in mail and plate

explanation.surface: Gear to protect a pilot who flies at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A night-fighter is a warplane, but 'say' tells you to hear it as a knight who fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal plate worn by medieval knights in battle as body protection.

clue.text: Such a scandal involving Irene Adler

definitions.text: Such a scandal involving Irene Adler

parts.words: Such a scandal involving Irene Adler
parts.note: Irene Adler is the woman in the Sherlock Holmes story A Scandal in ..., named after a central European kingdom

explanation.surface: A scandal surrounding a famous adventuress.
explanation.walkthrough: Conan Doyle's story 'A Scandal in Bohemia' features Irene Adler; the adjective describes such a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The scandal of Conan Doyle's story took place in Bohemia, so it is a scandal of that land.

clue.text: He invests in telescopic mirrors placed on an eminence

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: specula is the plural of speculum, a metal mirror in a reflecting telescope
a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

explanation.surface: A man puts money into telescope mirrors set on high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator is someone who puts money into ventures hoping for gain.

clue.text: Little Mary has one daughter blown up

parts.note: Little Mary is an old British euphemism for the stomach, the tum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl named Mary and her daughter are puffed up with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is old British slang for the belly, from a J. M. Barrie play.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid means swollen or distended, as a thing inflated is.

clue.text: Fish can change direction, maybe

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word can

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A fish might be able to turn round in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old synonym for possibly or perhaps.

clue.text: The Commons successfully defend these words of Dickens

parts.note: the Commons is the lower House of Parliament
to hold a position is to defend it successfully

explanation.surface: MPs hold firm in defence of what Dickens wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens edited a weekly magazine called Household Words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's weekly journal was titled Household Words, so these words are of that kind.

clue.text: Her husband voted for the Emperor

definitions.text: Her husband voted for the Emperor

parts.words: Her husband voted for the Emperor
parts.note: the princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor were electors; this is the title of such a prince's wife

explanation.surface: A woman whose husband backed the Emperor at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a German prince-elector of the Holy Roman Empire bore this title.

clue.text: Cough up, say, outside the Common Market for service Item

indicators.note: the sound-spelling goes round the Common Market's initials
say signals that cough up is to be spelt as it is heard

parts.note: cough up is respelt by its sound
EEC, the European Economic Community, was called the Common Market

explanation.surface: Pay up, someone says, out of the Common Market, for a service charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to spell 'cough up' as it sounds, and 'outside' splits that spelling round the Market's initials. 'Service' is a matching tea or coffee set, not a church service or a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is one piece of a coffee service, the matching set of crockery.

clue.text: Liqueur brandy left, for example, by Fielder

parts.note: fine is a French brandy, as in fine champagne
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Brandy is abandoned, say, by a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a fielding position in cricket, behind the batter on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leg is a cricket position, so it names the fielder standing there.

clue.text: Order of imperial Russia

parts.note: a decree issued by the tsar's government, with legal force

explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict issued by the Russian tsar.

clue.text: One more heart broken about a refusal

indicators.note: about places the jumbled letters round the word of refusal
broken tells us the letters of the word heart are scrambled

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Yet another broken heart over a rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles the heart into ATHER, and 'about' splits those letters round the refusal; the opening 'One' is part of the definition, not a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, one extra.

clue.text: A lucky chance, the tempest abating

parts.note: a tempest is a strong wind
abating means dropping or falling

explanation.surface: A stroke of luck: the storm is easing.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is an unexpected gain, a piece of good fortune.

clue.text: What's this I hear of your vacuum-cleaner?

definitions.text: What's this I hear of your vacuum-cleaner?

parts.words: What's this I hear of your vacuum-cleaner?
parts.note: the question sounds like gossip, but asks for the humming noise a running appliance makes

explanation.surface: A gossip asks about rumours concerning your vacuum cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the low buzzing hum of a motor spinning.

clue.text: The last edition is definitive

definitions.meaning: the newspaper's latest edition of the day

explanation.definitionFit: The day's closing print run of a paper bears this name, and a decision beyond appeal is conclusive.

clue.text: It expresses rising disgust

definitions.meaning: a rising is an uprising or rebellion
to disgust someone is to sicken or repel them

explanation.surface: Something that voices growing distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is an uprising, and to sicken a person is to repel them.

clue.text: Formerly seen in prison cells

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted within the words prison cells

explanation.surface: Former inmates were once spotted in jail cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some earlier time, in the past.

clue.text: I drink to North London borough

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore sling

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a district in the north of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLINGTON is a borough of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the boroughs making up Greater London.

clue.text: Love-note changed her colour

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
C is a musical note

indicators.note: changed tells us to rearrange the letters of the word her

explanation.surface: A love letter altered her complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellowish-brown pigment and shade.

clue.text: Sort of Army orderly

definitions.meaning: the standing professional army, as opposed to reserves

explanation.definitionFit: The full-time professional army is the Regular Army; anything orderly is evenly arranged.

clue.text: Submits to rudeness, -perhaps — there's no end to it

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the letters may be rearranged into another word
the last letter of the word rudeness is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with endless rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no end to it' drops the final S of RUDENESS; 'perhaps' rearranges RUDENES.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or tolerate, to put up with something.
